functions.get_item(sku): returns dict {sku:str, name:str, price:float in dollars, category:str} or None if sku unknown
functions.get_customer(customer_id): returns dict {id:str, name:str, discount:float fraction (0.10 means 10%), region:str} or None if unknown

value.notes: price = unit price in dollars (catalog price_cents/100), before customer discount. Discount is applied by invoice, not pricing. region and category are plain strings exactly as in the CSVs (region e.g. TX, OR, NY; category e.g. stationery, bags, food). Tax module takes region and category as inputs; tax rates are agent2's concern.

why: Defines the pricing interface used by invoice and tax so all three of us can code against it.

value: tax.compute_tax(region, lines, discount_pct) -> int. region: str|None (customer region code, e.g. "TX"; key in rates.csv). lines: list of {"category": str, "amount_cents": int} (one per invoice line, amount_cents = line total in cents, already quantity*unit price). discount_pct: number (percent, e.g. 10 for 10%; 0 if none). Returns total tax in integer cents, rounded half up once on the total. Taxable base = sum of amount_cents over lines whose category is not exempt, times (100-discount_pct)/100. tax = base * tax_pct / 100. Caller (invoice.py) gets lines and region/discount from pricing.py and calls tax only; invoice.py must not apply tax rules. tax.py raises KeyError for unknown region (see TAX_UNKNOWN_REGION).
why: Tax needs only region, line categories/amounts, and discount; it does not need pricing internals. Integer cents and percent numbers follow team standard. Single tax call on the invoice total follows RULES.md (tax on summed base, rounded once).

value: Unknown region code (not in data_tax/rates.csv) -> tax.compute_tax raises KeyError (team standard). region None or empty string means the customer is unknown / has no region -> tax is 0 (RULES.md: unknown customer pays 0% tax). Caller (invoice.py/pricing.py) passes region=None for an unknown customer; tax.py does not look up customers.
why: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0%, but team standard says failed lookups raise KeyError. Resolve by separating the two: unknown customer -> None -> 0 tax; unknown region code in a known customer's data -> KeyError (a data error, must not silently be taxed at 0).

value.money: decimal.Decimal in dollars, rounded to cents (ROUND_HALF_UP)
value.percent: multiplier applied to the base: 10% off -> 0.90; 8.25% tax -> 1.0825; 0% tax or no discount -> 1

why: Team standard: money as Decimal dollars, percents as multipliers. Makes the interface between pricing.py and tax.py unambiguous.

value.quote(customer_id: str, lines: list[tupl: lines = (sku, line_amount) for known SKUs only; discount = discount amount in dollars (already rounded). Returns (tax_amount rounded to cents ROUND_HALF_UP, tax_multiplier e.g. 1.0825 for 8.25%). Unknown customer -> (0.00, 1) i.e. 0%.

why: tax.py owns all tax rules, so it computes the tax base from lines and discount; invoice.py only displays the result.
